Zr4+ is a d0 cation that resists reduction by Li6PS5Cl, and the framework has no P, S, or Si oxyanion to form the sulfur-oxidation products that penalized the other coatings. Its very high Li/Zr ratio may shift the sulfide contact chemistry relative to Li2ZrO3 and Li6Zr2O7.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating oxyanion with good oxidative stability near 4 V. It is also chemically compatible with the sulfide electrolyte Li6PS5Cl, since its phosphate chemistry is close to the PS4 unit. As a Li-rich, non-redox coating it should suppress electron transfer and interfacial decomposition at the LiCoO2 interface.

LiAlO2 is a wide-gap Li-rich oxide whose Al3+ cation is hard to reduce, so it should resist redox reactions with the sulfide electrolyte and with LiCoO2 at 4 V. Its Li-O/Al-O chemistry is also unlikely to produce the sulfur-oxidation products (P2O5, SO2, SCl4) that penalized Li3PO4 contact.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 was insulating and had zero self-decomposition, but its contact with Li6PS5Cl gave reaction energy -0.337 eV/atom, penalty bin 16, not acceptable. The next coating should be a non-phosphate oxide with a more reduction-resistant cation.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, electrochemically inert fluoride that is thermodynamically stable against both LiCoO2 at 4 V and the sulfide electrolyte. Its F- anion is hard to oxidize, and it lacks the P, S, or Al cations that drove the sulfur-oxidation and reduction products seen with Li3PO4 and LiAlO2. It should therefore give a much smaller contact reaction energy than the oxide and phosphate coatings tested so far.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (contact penalty 0.337 eV, bin 16) and LiAlO2 (contact penalty 0.401 eV, bin 20) both reacted with Li6PS5Cl to form sulfur-oxidation or sulfate/chloride products, so both failed. Switching to a halide family tests whether a fluoride with no reducible or oxidizable cation gives a lower contact penalty.

proposal.hypothesis: LiNbO3 is a wide-gap Li-rich oxide with a d0 Nb5+ cation that is hard to reduce, so it should resist reaction with Li6PS5Cl. Unlike Li3PO4 and LiAlO2, it has no P or Al cation to form phosphate, sulfate, or chloride products. Nb-O coatings are also widely used as buffer layers at sulfide/oxide cathode interfaces.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (contact penalty 0.337 eV, bin 16), LiAlO2 (0.401 eV, bin 20), and LiF (0.310 eV, bin 15) all failed because the sulfide contact produced reduction or oxidation products. The next test is a d0 transition-metal oxide whose cation is less prone to reduction than Al3+.

proposal.hypothesis: Li4SiO4 is a wide-gap, Li-rich orthosilicate. Si4+ is a non-redox, hard-to-reduce cation, and the Li-rich, fully oxidized framework should avoid the sulfur-oxidation and sulfate/chloride products seen with the phosphate, Al-oxide and Nb-oxide contacts. It is also a silicate family not yet tested.
proposal.motivation: Earlier coatings from the phosphate (Li3PO4), Al-oxide (LiAlO2), fluoride (LiF) and Nb-oxide (LiNbO3) families all failed with Li6PS5Cl contact penalties of 0.29 to 0.40 eV/atom. Silicates have not been tried, so this explores a new chemical family.

proposal.hypothesis: LiCl is a wide-gap, electrochemically inert chloride. Its anion matches the Cl- in Li6PS5Cl, so it should avoid the sulfur-oxidation and P/Si/Al-oxyanion products that penalized the oxide and phosphate coatings. It is also a chloride, unlike the fluoride LiF that gave a penalty of 0.31 eV with LiPF6/S/SCl products, so it tests whether a Cl-anion coating lowers the contact penalty.
